method: General position-aware word chain, fitted on paragraph lines of the public practice training pages only, with no grammar, no meaning and no rule about word length. Fitted statistics: the distribution of line lengths; for each position class in a line (first word, interior, last word) the frequency of each word by its first glyph; and, per position class, how often each first glyph follows the previous word's last glyph (eva-basic glyphs). A line is written by drawing its length, drawing the first word from the line-initial words, then each next word by drawing its first glyph given the previous word's last glyph and its position class, and a word with that first glyph from that position class by frequency; a draw that would complete a manuscript four-word run is redrawn (seed 606, 3,000 lines). Any length difference comes only from the position-class word frequencies. On the practice split the fact holds on this text with whole lines kept (mean line-initial length 4.84 against 4.83 for the manuscript, beyond the within-line shuffle null) and fails when the same words are poured as a token stream (4.37).
